candidates.title: Weakened association between sequential phenological events corresponds to interphase extension
candidates.abstract: Seasonal events in temperate deciduous trees, from leaf-out to leaf fall, follow a fixed annual sequence. This study shows that the timing of consecutive events is statistically associated in European trees, but that the association between fruiting and leaf coloration has weakened in some species as the interval between these phases has increased. The sequential occurrence of leaf unfolding, flowering, fruiting, foliar senescence and other life-cycle events constitutes a full cycle of plant phenology. Temporal shifts in the seasonal timing of these phenophases have been regarded as key evidence of global environmental change. Most previous studies, however, have focused on the timing of individual phenophases. Little is known about the relationships between changes in timing across sequential phenophases. Here, using in-situ phenological records of major European tree species between 1980 and 2017, we show strong positive associations between consecutive phenophases. In particular, the statistical relationship between the timing of consecutive phenophases is comparable to that of temperature for spring phenological events and substantially exceeds the relationship with climatic factors for late-season phenological events. However, the associations themselves have shifted across years, with a significant decrease in the association between the timing of fruit ripening and autumnal coloration, corresponding to the largest extension of interphase duration. Current process-based phenological models largely overlook associations between consecutive phenological events and their interplay with climate change, potentially leading to biased projections of phenological changes and ecosystem adaptation to future climate change.

candidates.title: Discovering Underpotentially Deposited Crystalline Sodium Metal Nanoparticles on the Surface of Hard Carbon Anodes
candidates.abstract: Abstract Sodium-ion batteries are attractive candidates for low-cost and scalable energy storage in which hard carbon (HC) anodes are used. However, sodium (Na) metal plating in HC anodes at voltages above the plating potential remains a critical problem. The location and spatial distribution of crystalline sodium (c-Na) metal nanoparticles, the clusters associated with Na storage in HCs, are important for understanding this underpotential plating behavior but remain unclear. Here, we implement a cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and electron tomography (cryo-ET) workflow that directly localizes c-Na metal clusters in sodiated HC samples: cryo-ET maps nanoscale three-dimensional (3D) distributions, while cryo-EM resolves local structure and chemistry. Our workflow reveals that c-Na metal clusters reside predominantly on the surfaces or near surfaces of individual HC particles. This finding challenges existing interpretations in the literature that locate the c-Na metal clusters within closed nanopores in the bulk of the HC, presumably because prior characterization using nonimaging techniques and two-dimensional (2D) projection images associated with traditional transmission electron microscopy (TEM) lacks the spatial 3D information necessary to resolve the full spatial distribution. Our discovery is an important step toward explaining the underpotential plating phenomenon of Na metal in HC anodes, suggesting that particle-level surface and near-surface interfaces are relevant targets to mitigate plating alongside bulk-pore, electrode, and electrolyte/interphase design.

candidates.title: Solvation Cluster Engineering of Non-Fluorinated Ethers toward High-Energy Lithium Metal Batteries
candidates.abstract: Abstract Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) can provide high energy density for next-generation energy storage, yet their cycle life remains limited by interfacial incompatibility between electrolyte species and electrodes. Conventional electrolytes based on polar or fluorinated solvents often suffer from sluggish transport kinetics, high cost, and even environmental concerns. Herein, we rationally modulate the polarity and coordination ability of nonfluorinated solvents and report a fluorine-free host-guest synergy electrolyte (HGSE) constructed by tailoring the intermolecular interaction between a long-chain multidentate ether and a monodentate ether solvent. The weak Hδ+-Oδ- intermolecular interaction between these solvents tunes the electrolyte coordination ability and solvation cluster size, leading to a contact ion pair-dominated solvation cluster structure with enhanced ionic conductivity. Meanwhile, the optimized solvation cluster in HGSE promotes anion decomposition while suppressing electrode side reactions, resulting in anion-derived LiF-rich interphases and minimized cathode cracking. More notably, the HGSE electrolyte enables a Li||NCM811 pouch cell to deliver a high energy density of 472.5 Wh kg-1, while a 20 Ah-level anode-free Cu||Ni90 pouch cell with a lean electrolyte (1.5 g Ah-1) achieves a superior energy density of 525 Wh kg-1 with 71.6% capacity retention over 120 cycles. These findings elucidate the role of intermolecular interactions and solvation cluster engineering in high-energy and sustainable LMBs.

candidates.title: Machine Learning-Guided Precise Electrolyte Engineering Enables Stable Lithium Metal Pouch Cells Exceeding 350 Wh/kg at -40 °C
candidates.abstract: Abstract High-energy-density lithium metal batteries (LMBs) with wide-temperature adaptability are urgently needed for aerospace and military fields, yet extreme temperature conditions disrupt Li+ transport kinetics and cause failure in solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) chemistry regulation. To guide molecular selection for wide-temperature electrolyte design, we constructed Electrolyte-65K, a rule-defined library of electrolyte-relevant molecules, and trained D-P Compass using batch-computable molecular descriptors to efficiently predict and rank dipole moment (D) and polarizability (P). Applying the trained models to a literature-derived set of electrolyte molecule candidates, D-P Pareto analysis identified N,N-dimethyltrifluoromethanesulfonamide (DMTMSA) as the candidate at the Pareto knee. The thermally sensitive dipole-dipole interactions between DMTMSA and weakly solvating solvent 1,2-diethoxyethane (DEE) enable a temperature-autoresponsive electrolyte that maintains an anion-dominated solvation structure across a wide temperature range, enabling SEI chemistry engineering regulation from -40 to 60 °C. A 5.8 Ah pouch cell achieves a high energy density of 503.7 Wh kg-1 at 25 °C with a lifespan of 275 cycles and retains 365.5 Wh kg-1 at -40 °C with 99.8% capacity retention over 50 cycles. This work establishes a data-driven molecular screening framework for wide-temperature electrolyte engineering design.

candidates.title: Fine-Tuning Universal Machine Learning Potentials Enables Efficient Computation of Li Electrode Potentials in Battery Electrolytes
candidates.abstract: Abstract The electrode potential of Li metal is fundamental to the performance and stability of Li-metal batteries, yet its accurate prediction across diverse electrolyte chemistries remains a challenge. Standard quantum chemistry using cluster models fails to account for explicit bulk solvation, while ab initio molecular dynamics is restricted by the high computational cost of thermodynamic sampling. In this work, we present an integrated framework that combines a universal machine learning potential for electrolytes with a data-efficient fine-tuning strategy to compute Li electrode potentials. This workflow achieves ab initio level accuracy using ∼200 extra density functional theory calculations per electrolyte system. Furthermore, the identified relationship between local Li+ solvation environments and electrode potential shifts provides mechanistic insights into electrolyte-dependent redox behavior and offers guidance for rational electrolyte design.

candidates.title: Decoupled Proton and Oxygen Transport at Cathode Triple-Phase Interfaces via Noncovalently Cross-Linked Biomimetic Nanochannels
candidates.abstract: Abstract The performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) is critically governed by the cathodic triple-phase interface, where platinum catalyst poisoning and inefficient proton/oxygen transport severely impede the oxygen reduction reaction. Inspired by the selective transport of biological membranes, we herein develop a porphyrin-based organic network (H-PorBz) as a multifunctional ionomer modifier to reconfigure the catalyst/ionomer/gas triple-phase interface. In situ noncovalent cross-linking between the H-PorBz and Nafion via NH+-H···SO3- interactions forms an interfacial layer that decouples proton and oxygen transport while suppressing sulfonate-induced Pt poisoning. Spectroscopic and computational studies reveal that H-PorBz simultaneously enhances proton conduction and oxygen transport by establishing a low-barrier proton-transfer network and tuning nanopore polarity. This membrane-mimetic design reduces sulfonate coverage on Pt by 28% and oxygen-transport resistance by 39.4%, delivering a mass-specific power density of 15.8 W mgPt-1 under H2/air conditions, 1.7-fold that of a conventional Pt/C@Nafion cathode. The composite ionomer also demonstrates excellent durability (>120 h at 0.6 V), with a voltage decay rate below 50 μV h-1. This work presents a bioinspired interfacial engineering strategy that reconfigures the three-phase region to mitigate catalyst poisoning and transport losses, offering a viable route to high-performance low-Pt PEMFCs.

candidates.title: Lewis-Basic Metal Sulfide Electrode Interfaces Unlock High Power Density Alkaline All-Iron Redox Flow Batteries
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Alkaline all-iron redox flow batteries (AIRFBs) are promising for safe, low-cost grid-scale energy storage using Earth-abundant elements. However, insufficient energy efficiency and power density limit practical deployment, while the interfacial kinetic origin of these losses remains unclear. Here, we identify sluggish outer-sphere electron-transfer kinetics of Fe-chelate anolytes as a key kinetic bottleneck governing polarization in alkaline AIRFBs and further link this bottleneck to limited outer Helmholtz plane (OHP)-region accessibility and weak interfacial electronic coupling. To overcome this limitation, we develop Lewis-basic sulfide interfaces that regulate the local Fe-chelate/electrode environment. These regulated interfaces convert inefficient diffusion encounters into productive sulfide-assisted outer-sphere electron-transfer events, thereby accelerating anolyte redox kinetics and suppressing polarization. An alkaline AIRFB assembled with a Ni 3 S 4 -modified electrode delivers an energy efficiency of 80.65% at 200 mA cm -2 and a peak power density of 501.2 mW cm -2 , compared with 65.69% and 185.5 mW cm -2 for the pristine cell. The Ni 3 S 4 -based cell further maintains an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%, an average energy efficiency of 77.8%, and stable operation over 3000 cycles at 200 mA cm -2 . This work reveals an interfacial kinetic bottleneck in alkaline AIRFBs and establishes Lewis-basic interface engineering as a strategy for high-power and low-cost long-duration energy storage.

candidates.title: Breaking the Theoretical Capacity Limit of Fullerene Anode in Alkali-Ion Batteries Through Two-Dimensional Covalent Network Engineering
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon-based anode materials offer compelling advantages for rechargeable ion batteries, and particularly fullerene C 60 has a higher theoretical capacity of 446 mAh g -1 than the traditional graphite anode in lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, its zero-dimensional cage structure tends to spontaneously aggregate, and its alkali-metal intercalated intermediate (fulleride) facilely dissolves in organic electrolytes, severely limiting its practical anode capacity and deteriorating recyclability. Herein, for the first time, we apply metal-free two-dimensional C 60 covalent network (2D-C 60 ) with distinct bonding patterns, including tetragonal phase (TP-2D-C 60 ) and hexagonal phase (HP-2D-C 60 ) nanosheets, as novel anode materials for LIBs, achieving high anode capacity, breaking the theoretical limit of C 60 molecule. TP-2D-C 60 delivers a specific capacity of 522.0 mAh g -1 at 0.1 A g -1 , outperforming HP-2D-C 60 (408.6 mAh g -1 ) and pristine C 60 (3.4 mAh g -1 ). This phenomenon is rationalized by DFT calculations, revealing that TP-2D-C 60 exhibits a higher density of Li-ion binding sites and a lower Li-ion migration barrier than HP-2D-C 60 . To assess its universality across ion-battery chemistries, we further demonstrate the application of TP-2D-C 60 as an anode for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), achieving a high discharge capacity of 309.9 mAh g -1 at 0.1 A g -1 .

candidates.title: Mechanically-Driven Reconstruction of Lithium Metal for Stable All-Solid-State Batteries
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Dendrite growth at lithium-metal anode remains a critical bottleneck in sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). Current approaches often rely on alloy anodes that compromise energy density or artificial interlayers, introducing additional processing complexity. Herein, we show that accumulated deformation imposed by repeated folding and rolling mechanically reconstructs commercial Li from surface to bulk, replacing a rough carbonate-rich surface and mixed texture with a refined oxide-passivated surface and a strongly Li(200)-preferred texture. At low and medium folding degrees, surface refinement and renewal of the native passivation layer improve solid-solid contact and interfacial Li-ion transport, but remain insufficient to prevent short circuiting, whereas high-degree reconstruction drives texture homogenization, reduces spatial variations in local interfacial response, and synchronizes Li recession and advancement across the rigid Li | solid-state electrolyte interface. The synchronous interface motion suppresses differential recession and void formation during stripping, while mitigating dendritic Li growth during plating. As a result, Li | LPSCl 1.5 | NMC811 full cells achieve 79.3% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at C/2 rate, support 7.4 mA h cm -2 operation with 0.05% decay per cycle, and cycle stably below 0.5 MPa. These findings establish mechanical reconstruction as a direct materials-level strategy for stabilizing Li metal in sulfide-based ASSBs.

candidates.title: Copper Surface Engineering Enables Uniform Zn Plating in Zn Batteries at Unity N/P Ratio
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Zinc (Zn) metal plating is notoriously sensitive to interfacial inefficiencies under Zn-limited conditions, where small losses of active Zn rapidly lead to premature cell failure. Here, we demonstrate a surface reconstruction strategy for copper (Cu) current collectors that enables exceptional performance at a negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio of 1.0. By chemically etching Cu to create a sacrificial cuprous chloride (γ-CuCl) interface, we obtained a micro-textured Cu substrate with increased electrochemical surface area (ECSA). Upon initial electrochemical reduction, γ-CuCl converts to metallic Cu while releasing Cl - ions into the local interfacial region of the electrolyte. Density functional theory calculations indicate that localized Cl - ions favorably regulate Zn 2+ adsorption energy while suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction. Benefitting from the synergistic combination of enhanced ECSA and dynamic Cl - mediated interfacial engineering, Zn//Cu cells achieve stable plating/stripping cycling for 1654 h (69 days). Notably, Zn//MnO 2 full cells using 3D-printed etched Cu substrate assembled under a nominal N/P ratio of 1.0 (determined by a reversible capacity at 10 mA cm -2 ) deliver a remarkable device volumetric capacity of 53.5 mAh cm -3 . Under high-rate cycling (80 mA cm -2 ), the cell retains 70% of initial capacity over 500 cycles. This performance represents a benchmark for Zn reversibility under extreme material-limited conditions.

candidates.title: Intermetallic Anodes Unlock Bulk Aluminum Incorporation in Aqueous Batteries
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous aluminum-based batteries are attractive for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their development is limited by shallow Al utilization, surface passivation, hydrogen evolution, and sluggish anode kinetics. Here, we report an intermetallic-anode strategy that unlocks bulk Al incorporation through electrochemically driven Ni-Al alloying. Guided by alloying thermodynamics, Ni is identified as an effective Al host, and a high-surface-area Ni powder anode is constructed to make bulk alloying kinetically accessible beyond surface-limited deposition. The resulting Al-alloying Ni powder anode markedly reduces charge-transfer resistance and anode polarization, enabling stable symmetric-cell operation and long-duration full-cell cycling with a potassium nickel hexacyanoferrate cathode in a low-cost sulfate electrolyte, retaining 98.6% capacity after 6000 h at 0.1 mA cm -2 . When combined with electrolyte engineering, the full cell achieves 4000 cycles at 3 mA cm -2 with 76.6% capacity retention, while a pouch cell with 4 cm × 5 cm electrodes maintains 72.6% retention after 150 cycles. Mechanistic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal a Ni-assisted pathway that promotes uniform Al-containing deposition and improves the energetics of Al incorporation without intrinsically promoting hydrogen evolution. This work establishes intermetallic anodes as an active platform for bulk Al storage in practical aqueous batteries.

candidates.title: Beyond Isolated Active Sites: Adjacent Single-Atom-Nanoparticle Electronic Coupling Enables Lateral Lithium Growth
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise host regulation remains pivotal for dendrite-free lithium metal anodes (LMAs). While maximizing isolated single-atom sites improves initial Li nucleation, their uniform adsorption energetics inherently confine Li to these initial sites, favoring localized vertical accumulation over lateral growth. Here we propose an adjacent single-atom-nanoparticle electronic coupling strategy to break this thermodynamic bottleneck. Via coordination-mediated laser direct writing, we construct a hierarchical porous graphene host comprising ultrafine Co nanoparticles and adjacent Co single atoms. Precursor preorganization and the ultrafast, non-equilibrium kinetics of laser processing concurrently drive in situ graphitization and Co-species reconstruction, effectively suppressing the aggregation in conventional thermal synthesis. Mechanistically, rather than relying on isolated thermodynamic traps, interfacial electronic coupling reconstructs the local d -band center and establishes a directed spatial Li adsorption-energy gradient. This thermodynamic driving force compels Li to sequentially occupy neighboring sites, effectively precluding localized vertical accumulation. Owing to this spatially regulated deposition, the high-loading Li||LiFePO 4 full cells retain 71.4% capacity after 1000 cycles at 2 C. This adjacent electronic coupling strategy transcends the isolated active sites paradigm, opening a new dimension for interfacial electronic-structure regulation in practical LMAs.

candidates.title: Ionic-Ligand-Assisted Transport in Fluorinated Poly(ionic liquid) Electrolytes Enables 515 Wh Kg -1 Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Decoupling ionic conductivity from polymer segmental relaxation while maintaining interfacial stability remains a pivotal challenge for solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs). In this study, we construct an ionic-ligand-assisted transport framework by copolymerizing a fluorinated acrylate polymer with a poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) and optimizing the lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) salt concentration. Density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that cationic PIL moieties strongly anchor FSI - anions, creating anion-rich, spatially correlated coordination pathways that facilitate efficient Li + hopping. The optimized electrolyte exhibits a high ionic conductivity (0.38 mS cm -1 ) and an exceptional Li + transference number (0.77) at 30°C. The fluorinated backbone and PIL synergistically expand the oxidative stability window to 4.94 V and promote an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li-metal anode. Consequently, Li||Cu cells cycle stably for over 400 cycles with 99.1% average Coulombic efficiency. Solid-state Li||LiNi 0.9 Co 0.05 Mn 0.05 O 2 (NCM90) cells retain ≈81.0% capacity after 600 cycles at 4.3 V, and ≈83.1% capacity after 200 cycles at 4.5 V. Moreover, a high-energy-density (515 Wh kg -1 ) solid-state pouch cell with an ultrathin Li anode (50 μm) and a high-loading NCM90 cathode (≈56 mg cm -2 ) delivers stable cycling and exceptional safety. This ionic-ligand regulation paradigm provides critical mechanistic insights for designing high-performance and high-safety solid-state batteries.

candidates.title: Ion-Electron Convergent Interphases Enable Ultrahigh Sulfur Utilization for All-Solid-State Li-S Batteries
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT All-solid-state batteries offer a safer route toward electrochemical energy storage with high energy density, but the active-material utilization is commonly limited by unbalanced carrier transport dynamics through spatially decoupled delivery pathways, which overlap only at restricted reaction fronts. Such an issue is particularly severe for electronically and ionically insulating sulfur/Li 2 S, making efficient sulfur conversion the key bottleneck for practical all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs). Here, we propose surface-bound ion-electron convergent interphases on the Li 2 S surface that reconstruct localized triple-phase contacts into an integrated active surface. Using the effective magnetic moment, originating from spin asymmetry, as a screening criterion for interfacial affinity, Li 2 FeS 2 is identified to form a robust surface-bound interphase with Li 2 S, which bridges separated ion and electron pathways at the reaction areas, decreasing the transport tortuosity and lowering the activation barriers for both Li 2 S oxidation and reduction. Consequently, ASSLSBs stably work over 10 000 cycles at 1 mg cm -2 while delivering a loading-insensitive sulfur utilization of 97.8% and 95.8% at 1 and 8 mg cm -2 , respectively. Moreover, a record areal capacity of 38.69 mAh cm -2 is achieved, highlighting the spatially surface-bound mixed conductors as an effective design principle for synchronizing coupled ion-electron transfer (CIET) in all-solid-state batteries.

candidates.title: Fundamental Design Principles and Engineering Strategies of Liquid-Phase Electrolytes for Highly Durable Rechargeable Lithium Metal Batteries
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li) metal has emerged as the premier anode candidate in next-generation high-energy-density batteries due to its ultrahigh theoretical capacity and ultralow electrochemical potential. However, critical technical barriers persist in Li metal anode implementation, such as uncontrolled Li dendrite growth and persistent interfacial side reactions. Acting as the mediating agent between cathodes and anodes, electrolytes critically determine battery overall performance. Taking solvent-salt-additive components as the entry point, adopting liquid-phase electrolyte engineering strategies to optimize electrolyte composition and regulate solvation structure can not only address the inherent issues of Li metal anodes, but also endow Li metal batteries with desired performances, including high safety, high-voltage tolerance, fast-charging capability, and wide-temperature operation. In this review, the design principles of reliable liquid-phase electrolytes for Li metal batteries are discussed in detail. The essential liquid-phase electrolyte engineering strategies, including designing new-type salt/solvent molecular architectures, restructuring salt-solvent combination systems, incorporating electrolyte additives with various functions, utilizing (localized) high-concentration electrolytes, and developing brand-new electrolyte formulations for adapting to different temperature ranges, are comprehensively summarized. Moreover, emerging design strategies, future design considerations, and remaining challenges in electrolyte engineering are highlighted, with the aim of pointing out potential opportunities to propel the practical development of Li metal batteries.

candidates.title: 16.52% Efficiency All-Inorganic Perovskite Solar Cells via Al-Doped ZnO/SnO 2 Electron Transport Bilayer for Improved Interfacial Energy-Level Alignment
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial energy-level misalignment in all-inorganic perovskite solar cells generally causes inefficient charge extraction. Here, we propose an Al-doped ZnO (AZO)/SnO 2 electron transport bilayer to improve energy-level alignment in CsPbI 2 Br-based PSCs. By this approach, we achieved a champion efficiency of 16.52%, which is the highest reported value for all-inorganic CsPbI 2 Br PSCs without doping or passivation of the perovskite, along with a high V OC of 1.33 V. AZO-based devices substantially outperform ZnO-based controls, delivering a PCE of 16.52% versus 15.21%, with suppressed dark current, reduced trap density, lower non-radiative recombination, and smaller hysteresis. The AZO device retains 80% of its initial efficiency after 662 h of continuous illumination, compared with only 312 h for the ZnO counterpart. Al 3+ substitution for Zn 2+ elevates the ZnO conduction band minimum, establishing a favorable cascade alignment among SnO 2 /AZO/perovskite that lowers the electron extraction barrier and blocks hole backflow. Al doping also suppresses oxygen vacancies, reducing interfacial trap-state density and enhancing perovskite crystallinity. Efficient charge extraction further suppresses Ag electrode degradation and corrosion, contributing to long-term stability. This work establishes a rational interfacial engineering approach using an AZO/SnO 2 bilayer for efficient and stable all-inorganic perovskite solar cells.

candidates.title: Mechanochemically Disordered Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 Oxyhalide Unlocks Superionic Conductivity (>10 mS.cm -1 )
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT All-solid-state lithium-metal batteries (ASSBs) offer a promising route to surpass the energy-density limits of conventional lithium-ion technology. However, their commercialization is hindered by interfacial instability, chemo-mechanical degradation, and the limited ionic conductivity of current solid electrolytes, driving the search for new fast-ion conductors, particularly among lithium oxyhalides. Here, we report a new lithium tantalum oxychloride, Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 , synthesized via a simple low-temperature route. The material crystallizes in a triclinic structure composed of isolated [Ta 2 OCl 10 ] 2- dimers and exhibits a room-temperature ionic conductivity of 0.002 mS.cm - 1 . Ball milling dramatically enhances Li + transport, increasing the conductivity by a factor of 5000 to 11 mS.cm -1 while reducing the activation energy from 0.46 to 0.27 eV. Combined structural, spectroscopic, and computational analyses reveal that this enhancement originates from the formation of a highly disordered, liquid-like Li + sublattice. Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 further demonstrates a stability window of 1.89-3.70 V vs. Li x In and enables ASSBs with low polarization and excellent capacity retention (700 cycles at 1C with decay less than 20%). These results establish Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 as a promising superionic conductor and highlight the Li-M-O-Cl family as a fertile design space for next-generation solid electrolytes.

candidates.title: Chloride-Mediated Activation of Aluminum-Alloyed Liquid Metal Anodes for Stretchable Asymmetric Energy Storage
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Gallium-based liquid metals are attractive anodes for stretchable energy storage because they operate dendrite-free, yet their bulk faradaic capacity remains locked behind a native oxide shell that conventional electrolytes cannot remove. Here, this passivation problem is resolved through the co-design of an aluminum-alloyed gallium-indium (AlGaIn) anode and a chloride-rich water-in-ionic-liquid (WIL) electrolyte, and the indium-assisted electrochemical activation mechanism connecting them is identified. Al alloying converts the native oxide into a hydroxyl-rich mixed Al-Ga-O shell susceptible to [GaCl 4 ] - -mediated etching, while the In(III) ions preferentially reduced into metallic patches that seed reversible Ga alloying/dealloying within the WIL. Potential-resolved ex situ XPS indicates that in conventional TFSI-based electrolytes, the electrode passivates beneath a TFSI-derived interphase, whereas in the WIL, a chloride-dominated electrode-electrolyte interphase forms instead. The activated anode gains 60% capacity during activation and retains ∼100% capacity over 1600 cycles at 500 mA g - 1 . Paired with a sonochemically derived GaOOH nanosheet cathode in a stretchable asymmetric cell, the asymmetric full cell delivers a maximum of 66.28 mWh cm -3 normalized to the active-electrode volume, and 90% capacity retention over 4000 cycles. The halide-mediated oxide-displacement principle established here provides a generalizable electrolyte-design strategy for oxide-passivated liquid-metal and post-lithium anodes.

candidates.title: Bifunctional Additive Enabled Thermoresponsive Electrolytes With Dual-Mode Manipulation Toward Safe Lithium Metal Batteries
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal safety issues arising from electrolyte instability at elevated temperatures pose a critical challenge for lithium (Li) metal batteries (LMBs). Thermoresponsive electrolytes offer a promising solution, yet battery systems with high-rate capability and reliable thermal protection have not been realized. Herein, we introduce a bifunctional LiNO 3 additive into a high-volume-fraction vinylene carbonate-based thermoresponsive electrolyte (HVCE-N) to enhance the performance of LMBs at room and elevated temperatures. Notably, the introduction of the LiNO 3 additive modifies the solvation structure of Li + and forms a Li 3 N/LiN x O y solid electrolyte interface with high ionic conductivity. Under thermal shock, HVCE-N undergoes a rapid liquid-to-solid phase transition upon free radical polymerization to form a polymer network. More importantly, LiNO 3 can regulate the free radical concentration to control the degree of polymerization, thereby preserving high ion transport capability even after phase transition. As a result, a Li||NCM811 cell based on HVCE-N exhibits high-rate performance from 1C to 10C, and stable cycling at 100°C. When subjected to a thermal shock of 200°C, HVCE-N suppresses thermal runaway for Li||NCM811 pouch cell. This electrolyte design offers a new strategy to develop highly safe LMBs with high-rate performance.

candidates.title: Redirecting Bond Cleavage in Sacrificial Prelithiation via Dual-Side Separator Engineering for Anode-Free Lithium Batteries
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Anode-free lithium metal batteries (AFLMBs) promise extreme gravimetric and volumetric energy densities but suffer from irreversible active lithium loss, sluggish desolvation kinetics, and dendritic proliferation. Herein, we report a catalyst-induced bond-cleavage redirection concept to unlock efficient sacrificial prelithiation, implemented via a dual-side functionalized separator. On the cathode side, a 5 μm MoC 1-x /NC-0.3Co coating redirects Li 2 C 2 O 4 decomposition from high-barrier Li-O cleavage to preferential C─C bond scission. Theoretical calculations and operando characterizations confirm this mechanistic shift, lowering the delithiation potential to 3.79 V at 60°C with a 99.5% Li + utilization rate. To safeguard the liberated lithium inventory against depletion, the anode side integrates a PSSLi-PFPE bilayer. This coating accelerates Li + desolvation and drives the in-situ construction of a LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase, enabling Li symmetric cells cycling for over 1700 h (1.0 mAh cm -2 , DOD = 80.7%). Bridging fundamental bond kinetics with practical engineering, the assembled 1.0 Ah anode-free pouch cell (NCM811||MoC 1-x /NC-0.3Co-LCO/PE/PSSLi-PFPE||Cu) achieves gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 458.6 Wh kg -1 and 1005.2 Wh L -1 , a power output of 989.1 W kg -1 , retaining 80.1% capacity after 100 cycles. This non-invasive separator strategy provides a unified framework connecting bond kinetics to practical cell manufacturing, charting a feasible avenue for high-energy AFLMBs.

candidates.title: Sustainable Biomass-Based Fiber Materials as Structural and Functional Scaffolds for Advanced Metal Batteries
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Biomass-based fiber materials, including cellulose, chitosan, bacterial cellulose, and their derivatives, have emerged as a distinctive class of structural and functional scaffolds, effectively bridging renewable materials chemistry with advanced energy storage technologies. This review systematically elucidates their hierarchical structural characteristics, classifications, and the intrinsic structural-function-application relationships that underpin their versatility. Furthermore, the critical roles of these materials as key components-including solid-state/liquid electrolytes, separators, electrodes, and binders-in various metal battery systems, particularly lithium- and zinc-based batteries, are comprehensively summarized. The discussion further highlights how the rational architectural design of biomass-derived fibrous materials can significantly enhance ionic conductivity, interfacial stability, and mechanical integrity. By improving these fundamental properties, such materials provide effective strategies for addressing major challenges, including dendrite formation and cycling instability. Finally, the current challenges and future research perspectives are discussed, with particular emphasis on precise molecular-level design, scalable fabrication technologies, and standardized evaluation protocols, all of which are essential for advancing the development of next-generation green and sustainable energy storage devices.

candidates.title: Solvent-Free Metal-Organic Framework-Based Porous Liquid Electrolyte for Ultrahigh-Temperature (180°C) Zn Metal Batteries
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Zn metal batteries capable of withstanding ultrahigh temperatures are urgently needed across diverse fields, yet their development is hindered by the poor thermal adaptability of conventional electrolytes. Herein, we develop an innovative electrolyte paradigm represented by a metal-organic framework (MOF)-based porous liquid electrolyte (PLE) without active organic or H 2 O solvents, which enables long-term operation of Zn metal batteries at 180°C for the first time. Modeled on UiO-66, PLE combines permanent microporosity with liquid fluidity, offering non-flammability, thermal stability, and anode compatibility. The permanent micropores of the UiO-66 skeleton provide ordered nanoconfined ion transport channels, while flexible grafted polymeric chains offer coordination-dissociation hopping sites, and ultimately suppress dendrite growth even at high temperatures. Zn||Zn symmetric cells deliver ultra-long cycling lifespans of 10 000 h at 25°C, 4000 h at 120°C, 2100 h at 150°C, and 600 h at 180°C, far surpassing state-of-the-art Zn battery electrolytes. Zn||V 2 O 5 batteries deliver stable performance across 25-180°C. Moreover, the pore structure of PLE effectively adsorbs polyiodides and polysulfides, enabling high-temperature Zn||I 2 batteries and, remarkably, extending to Li||S (80°C) and Li||V 2 O 5 batteries (180°C). This work enriches the design philosophy of functional electrolytes and breaks the long-standing temperature barrier of metal batteries.

candidates.title: Breaking the Polarity-Coordination Coupling in Electrolyte Design for High-Voltage Lithium Batteries (Adv. Energy Mater. 40/2026)
Diagnosing the Role of Mn Additives in Aqueous Zn/MnO 2 Batteries
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Manganese dioxides are pervasive as cathode materials for aqueous zinc-ion batteries; however, their energy storage mechanism has proven to be complex. Increasing evidence suggests that Mn dissolution contributes to cathode capacity via a reversible dissolution-redeposition process, in addition to capacity from Zn 2+ /H + (de)intercalation. Understanding the role played by Mn 2+ in the electrolyte, particularly when introduced as an electrolyte additive, is important for diagnosing cathode degradation. Using operando X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectroscopy, we track Mn 2+ in operating cells to gain insights into the complexity of the MnO 2 cathode. While some suppression of cathode dissolution by the additive cannot be excluded, our measurements suggest that Mn 2+ electrolyte additives improve cycling performance by supplying extra redox-active Mn during charge, rather than solely by suppressing Mn dissolution, thereby compensating for cathode degradation. Benefiting from operando XRF, we propose that a potential contributor to capacity fading is the incomplete dissolution of the MnO 2 cathode and incomplete redeposition of Mn 2+ from the electrolyte, and that this fading does not appear to be mitigated by using Mn 2+ additives. These findings underscore the necessity of directly tracking Mn 2+ evolution, and that improving reversibility requires addressing both the dissolution of MnO 2 and the redeposition of Mn 2+ .

candidates.title: Constructing an Adaptive Flexible Interphase on Halide Electrolytes by Lewis-Acid-Induced Polymerization for High-Voltage All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT All-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) combining halide solid electrolytes (HSEs) with high-nickel layered oxide cathodes offer great promise for high energy density, yet they suffer from severe interfacial issues such as oxidative decomposition, mechanical degradation, and chemical incompatibility with sulfide electrolytes. Herein, we report a Lewis-acid-induced surface-softening strategy that constructs a nanoscale adaptive flexible interphase (AFI) via in situ polymerization of acrylonitrile (AN) on a representative halide electrolyte, Li 3 InCl 6 (LIC). The resulting AFI layer concurrently provides ionic conductivity, excellent oxidation stability (>4.8 V), and favorable viscoelasticity, thereby synergistically enhancing the electrochemical, chemical, and mechanical stability of the interface without compromising bulk ion transport. When paired with a single-crystal ultrahigh-nickel cathode LiNi 0.94 Co 0.05 Mn 0.01 O 2 (Ni94), the surface-softened LIC (S-LIC) enables ASSLBs delivering specific capacities of 223.8 and 209.5 mAh g -1 at 2 C and 4 C, respectively, retaining over 85% of the initial capacity after 2000 cycles at 2 C, and operate stably for more than 9000 cycles at 10 C. Even under an ultrahigh cutoff voltage of 4.8 V, a capacity retention of 81% is achieved after 800 cycles at 2 C. This work provides a broadly applicable and efficient interfacial engineering route for high-voltage halide-based ASSLBs.

candidates.title: Locally Competitive Coordination Electrolyte for High-Voltage Lithium-Metal Batteries With Ni-Rich Cathodes
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li) metal anodes (LMAs) hold great promise to increase the energy density of batteries. This is especially true when using an energy-dense cathode such as Ni-rich layered transition metal oxides, but unfortunately, these lead to accelerated capacity loss when combined with LMAs. Ni-rich cathodes suffer from surface reduction, which can be accelerated in contact with certain electrolyte solvents. This in turn leads to transition metal dissolution and shuttling, which poisons the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and complicates the anode stabilization. Here, we propose nitrile primary solvent combined with ether co-solvent, diluent and two borate salts to suppress parasitic reaction. A competition in the ion coordination between solvents surrounded by diluents is achieved. This leads to the anions being preferentially decomposed in the SEI and enhanced reversibility. Using high cathode areal capacity (4.0 mAh cm - 2 ), thin LMAs (N/p = 2.5), lean electrolyte (3 g Ah - 1 ), and high charging voltages (≥4.4 V), we achieve a capacity retention of 80% over 250 cycles. With moderately high loading cathode (3.4 mAh cm - 2 ) but higher upper voltage (4.6 V), the cells retain 87.5% capacity retention over 430 cycles. Finally, we demonstrate Ah-level anode-free pouch cells with a 78.7% capacity retention over 100 cycles.

candidates.title: Operando X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Reveals Oxide Solid Electrolyte Stability against Electrochemically Plated Lithium
candidates.abstract: Abstract X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) has revealed many possible Li-induced interfacial reactions in solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), but most in situ studies form Li|electrolyte interfaces through non-electrochemical Li deposition, including evaporation, sputtering, or electron-beam-induced deposition. These routes may introduce additional energy that activates reaction pathways not accessed during electrochemical Li plating. Here, we use lab-based operando XPS to directly evaluate oxide solid-state electrolyte stability during electrochemical Li formation. Using this approach, we find sharply different responses for two representative oxide SSEs: NASICON-type Li1+xAlxTi2-x(PO4)3 (LATP) is reduced upon Li plating, forming a Li+/Ti3+-rich mixed-conducting interphase that partially relaxes through coupled ionic-electronic redistribution, whereas garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) shows no spectroscopically resolvable Zr or La reduction. This work represents the first direct operando XPS evaluation of SSE stability against electrochemically plated Li metal.

candidates.title: Operando Raman Spectroscopy-Guided 24-Hour Aging Assessment of Activated Carbon Positive Electrodes for Lithium-Ion Capacitors
candidates.abstract: Abstract While high-power lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) with high energy density emerge as promising pulse-/peak-power solutions for AI data centers, their long-term viability remains severely hindered by the degradation of the activated carbon (AC) positive electrode. To evaluate this aging behavior, we propose a 24-h high-voltage cycling (HVC) protocol integrated with operando Raman spectroscopy, demonstrating that the turning point in the D1 band can serve as a sensitive indicator of corrosion severity. During the early-stage HVC aging, cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI) formation and gas evolution passivate defect-related Raman signals, narrowing the D1 band. As aging proceeds, carbon corrosion becomes dominant and broadens the D1 band. By validating this approach across various ACs, we establish a direct correlation between an earlier structural turning point and accelerated capacity decay, thereby uncovering carbon aging mechanisms and offering an unprecedented, rapid diagnostic technique for capacitor-type materials.

candidates.title: A 2.2 V Aqueous Redox Flow Battery Enabled by Passive pH Decoupling
candidates.abstract: Abstract Aqueous redox flow batteries (ARFBs) comprising earth-abundant charge carriers could cheaply store grid-scale renewable electricity, but most lab-scale systems have a low open-circuit potential (OCP) that inflates system cost. We report a non-hybrid aqueous flow cell with an OCP of 2.2 V, among the highest reported for this class, pairing an alkaline chromium-1,3-propylenediaminetetraacetate negolyte with an acidic bromide posolyte. The two electrolytes maintain an approximately seven-unit pH gradient across a single cation-exchange membrane, without external oxygen or a bipolar-membrane recovery sub-cell: operando pH measurements and a zero-dimensional model show that the difference is sustained passively by balancing slow proton crossover against hydrogen evolution and positive-side acid generation. The cell cycles for 240 h with a Coulombic efficiency of up to 99.5%; tuning the posolyte additive, electrode, and membrane raises the peak power density to 534 mW cm-2 at 43 °C.

candidates.title: Constructing Hybrid Solid-Liquid Li+ Transport Networks for Fast-Charging Thick Electrodes
candidates.abstract: Abstract Fast-charging technology for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries remains constrained by high interfacial impedance and sluggish Li+ transport within electrodes. Herein, hierarchical-sized Li1.5Al0.5Ti1.5(PO4)3 (LATP, particle ranging from 5 to 500 nm) is used to construct a hybrid solid-liquid Li+ transport network in high-mass-loading cathodes (27 mg cm-2). A combination of different characterization techniques is employed to understand the underlying working principle of LATP from the particle to the electrode scale. LATP nanograins (∼10 nm) adsorbed onto cathode particle surfaces reduce Li+ desolvation energy (43.30 vs 52.97 kJ mol-1) and stabilize a thin CEI after cycling. Submicron LATP particles (320-480 nm) infiltrate pores of thick electrodes, forming interconnected networks that increase the Li+ diffusion coefficient. Furthermore, LATP increases the Li+ transference number of the liquid electrolyte within LATP-permeated regions. Consequently, LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||Li cells with LATP-blended cathodes deliver dramatically enhanced rate performance (102 vs 36 mAh g-1 at 0.75C and -10 °C).

candidates.title: Ultralow Deposition Potential and Antisite-Boosted Diffusivity of Li3Ga2 Anode for All-Solid-State Batteries
candidates.abstract: Abstract Existing alloy anodes suffer from high redox potentials and sluggish Li atomic kinetics, limiting the energy density and rate capability of all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs). Herein, we report a well-designed Li3Ga2 alloy anode that simultaneously delivers an ultralow Li deposition potential (0.007 V vs. Li+/Li) and fast Li atomic diffusion kinetics (2.0 × 10-8 cm2 s-1). The high Li atomic diffusivity primarily originates from moderate Li/Ga antisite mixing, stabilizing the anode-solid electrolyte interface and enabling a high critical current density of 24 mA cm-2 in ASSLBs. Coupled with a LiCoO2 cathode, the ASSLB delivers a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 96.5% and an ultralong cycle life of 2000 cycles at room temperature, with a high output voltage of 3.84 V, outperforming state-of-the-art alloy-based counterparts. A practical all-solid-state pouch cell employing the LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cathode also delivers outstanding cycling stability. This work redefines alloy anode design principles through synergistic optimization of Li deposition potential and Li atomic diffusivity.
